title: Homotopically surjective simplicial-presheaf model map
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; the model-category conventions used below are stated explicitly in this node. Categories are complete and cocomplete, weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three and retract closure, and (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and factorizations of all arrows; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Cofibrant and fibrant mean that the initial and terminal maps, respectively, are cofibrations and fibrations. A cofibrant replacement is a trivial fibration $QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant; a fibrant replacement is a trivial cofibration $X\to TX$ with $TX$ fibrant. Combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets $I,J$ whose right lifting classes are the trivial fibrations and fibrations, respectively. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated, for some regular $\kappa$, under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A Quillen adjunction is an ordinary adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It is a Quillen equivalence when, for each cofibrant source object $A$ and fibrant target object $Y$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Write $\mathsf{sSet}$ for the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with the Kan model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms; fibrations have the right lifting property against all horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$), where $\Delta^n$ is the representable simplex and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of its faces other than the $i$th; weak equivalences induce a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups of geometric realizations. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial. There exist a small ordinary category $D$ and a Quillen adjunction $L_0:\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R_0$, where $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ has the projective model structure (objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and cofibrations defined by the left lifting property against trivial fibrations), such that for every fibrant $X$ in $\mathcal M$ and every cofibrant replacement $q:QR_0X\to R_0X$, the counit composite $L_0QR_0X\xrightarrow{L_0q}L_0R_0X\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_X}X$ is a weak equivalence. A Quillen adjunction with this counit property is called homotopically surjective.
